To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the new generation of heat exchangers will have a header size ratio of 1:2.5 and the header height will be 1.5 times the tube height.
the header design has a significant impact on the performance of the entire heat exchangers, and that the optimum header size ratio is 0.4 for the integrated heat exchangers studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the heat exchanger header and tubes for new generations of heat exchange modules.
the design of the header of the heat exchanger module and the optimization of the entire module performance.
the design and optimization of new generations of air-cooled heat exchangers with integrated headers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new generation of air cooled heat exchange modules can be significantly improved by optimizing the header size and the tube size ratio.
for the same tube size, the optimum header size ratio is 0.3 and the optimum header height to tube length ratio is 0,2.
for the 1 kW module, the optimum header size ratio is 0.5 and 0.6 for the two header configurations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new 3-D CFD simulation approach is developed to simulate the performance of the inlet and outlet header of air-cooled heat exchanger modules and then integrated with the performance of the tubes.
we have developed a new design optimization methodology for integrated heat exchanger modules for new generation of air cooled heat exchange units.

we have developed a 3D CTD model to simulate the header pressure drop, and then we have developed a new solver to evaluate the performance of the entire heat exchangers based on the information of the header pressure drop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a new generation air cooled heat exchanger can be designed to achieve a 10% reduction in the ratio of header frontal area to heat exchanger frontal area.
it is possible to design an integrated heat exchanger that has a very small header size and still achieve a very small pressure drop.
a 1 kW integrated air cooled heat exchanger module can be designed with a header size ratio less than 0.5 with a pressure drop less than 0 psi.
